name: redact-entities
summary: Redact person, organization, and location mentions from free text using text.detect-entities' real DistilBERT-NER forward pass.
description: Runs the exact same tokenize -> DistilBERT-NER forward pass -> BIO-decode pipeline as text.detect-entities (registry#465, dslim/distilbert-NER, Apache-2.0), reused directly via a source-level dependency rather than duplicated, then substitutes a bracketed placeholder ("[PER]", "[ORG]", "[LOC]", "[MISC]") for each detected entity span instead of returning raw entity data -- copying everything else through unchanged. A real model forward pass at execution time, not a keyword list or regex-based masking. Second pick (after audio.transcribe-speech@1.1.0's VAD gate, registry#477) from a post-#473 downstream-capability review of this session's shipped model engines: no new model, no new license/verification burden -- same weight table, same license record as text.detect-entities. A new capability id, not a version of text.detect-entities, since "redact" is a genuinely different action from "detect" for a caller (different intent, different output shape), not a refinement of the same one. Inherits text.detect-entities' documented model limitation faithfully: this compact model sometimes tags an interior WordPiece of a multi-piece entity with a fresh B- tag instead of a continuing I-, which the shared BIO merge (correctly) reports as separate adjacent spans -- so a name like 'Acme Corp' can come back partially redacted as '[ORG][ORG][ORG]' rather than one '[ORG]', verified directly against the real model rather than assumed. Does not detect speech, translate, resolve entities against a knowledge base, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow.

use_cases.scenario: As a privacy export reviewer, I want person, organization, and location mentions blanked out of a document before it leaves a privacy boundary, so that a forwarded support ticket or shared transcript doesn't carry PII a vendor or auditor shouldn't see.

input_example.text: Sarah Chen from Acme Corp will follow up with the Berlin team next week.

output_example.redacted_text: [PER] from [ORG][ORG][ORG] will follow up with the [LOC] team next week.

use_cases.scenario: As a privacy export reviewer, I want a well-known person and organization consistently redacted even when the model tags them as several adjacent spans, so that no fragment of a detected entity leaks through unredacted.

input_example.text: Elon Musk founded SpaceX in California.

use_cases.scenario: As a privacy export reviewer, I want text with no detected entities returned completely unchanged, so that redaction never alters content that doesn't need it.

input_example.text: The quarterly report is due next Friday.

output_example.redacted_text: The quarterly report is due next Friday.

preconditions.description: Caller supplies a text string (may be empty).

postconditions.description: Every byte of the input not covered by a detected entity span appears unchanged, in order, in redacted_text; each detected span is replaced by exactly one bracketed placeholder ([PER]/[ORG]/[LOC]/[MISC]).
Identical input yields identical output within one WASM instantiation. Cross-instantiation / cross-host-architecture byte-identity is NOT proven -- see risk.determinism_class.

side_effects.description: Produces a redacted string in memory; does not log, persist, or transmit input text.

provenance.author: enricopiovesan
provenance.spec_ref: registry#481, second pick from the post-#473 'Five Engines, What Next' downstream-capability review, after audio.transcribe-speech@1.1.0's VAD gate (#477). Reuses text.detect-entities' (#465) DistilBERT-NER engine directly via a source-level path dependency on that crate's new lib.rs (split out of its single main.rs the same way audio-detect-speech-segments was split for #477) -- no new model, no new verification burden.

authoring.test_evidence: capability-src/text-redact-entities: 10 #[test] cases (placeholder label mapping, single-span and multiple-non-overlapping-span substitution, no-entities passthrough, defensive handling of an out-of-order/invalid span, full-pipeline determinism and empty-input handling, well-formed output shape, missing-text-field default) against text.detect-entities' own exposed fixture_model() (that crate's own main.rs was split into a lib.rs + thin bin the same way audio-detect-speech-segments was for registry#477, so this capability reuses its engine directly rather than duplicating it -- text.detect-entities@1.0.0's published contract/artifact is untouched by that source-only refactor, verified by re-running all 19 of its pre-existing tests unchanged); cargo llvm-cov functions=100%, lines=100%, regions=100%. Verified against the real published model via the compiled wasm32-unknown-unknown --features full-model artifact under wasmtime on real sentences: 'Sarah Chen from Acme Corp will follow up with the Berlin team next week.' redacts to '[PER] from [ORG][ORG][ORG] will follow up with the [LOC] team next week.', and 'Elon Musk founded SpaceX in California.' redacts to '[PER][PER] founded [ORG][ORG] in [LOC].' -- both correctly reproducing text.detect-entities' own documented BIO-fragmentation behavior on these exact sentences (verified directly against the real model, not assumed to carry over). License: same as text.detect-entities -- dslim/distilbert-NER is Apache-2.0, verified directly against the model's Hugging Face API metadata.
